### Investment Memo: INSM — 25 November 2026

**Verdict**: HOLD (deal-bound) — existing holders collect $175; **do not initiate new positions** | Conviction: Medium
**Price Target**: $175.00 (the Sanofi cash consideration; +2.9% from current $170.15) | Standalone break value: **$105–120** (−30% to −38%)
**Time Horizon**: To deal close, expected H1 2027 (~6–7 months)

---

**Investment Thesis**

On 24-Nov-2026 Sanofi agreed to acquire Insmed for **$175.00/share all-cash (~$41.0B, ~46% premium, ~27x TTM sales)**, with committed financing, no financing condition, and an H1-2027 close. INSM is therefore no longer a biotech growth stock — it is a **merger-arbitrage claim** whose payoff is +2.85% if the deal closes and roughly −30% (to the $119.80 undisturbed price) if it breaks. At the market-implied ~92% completion probability, expected return over ~7 months is **≈0% versus ~2.6% on T-bills** — the position is dominated by cash, and all 11 specialists agree there is no fundamental alpha left for INSM shareholders: the excellence of the franchise is precisely why Sanofi paid up, and that value has already been collected.

---

**Key Findings by Domain**

- **Macro & Sector**: Sector structurally attractive (86.7% peer median GM, ~14% market CAGR, category creation in NCFB) — but explicitly *not* a stock call post-deal. Macro is unfavourable for biotech (CPI 3.82%, 10Y 5.13%, real 10Y ~3.0%) yet largely irrelevant to a fixed $175 cash claim; residual exposure is rate/carry: the 2.85% spread pays only ~50–100bp over bills. Watch Sanofi's $35B bridge take-out if credit spreads keep widening.
- **Geopolitical & Legal**: Risk rating **MEDIUM**. No hotspot exposure (~90% revenue US/Japan/EU). The legal risk is deal mechanics: HSR + EU/Japan/UK clearances (low substantive overlap — no NCFB competitor at Sanofi), §14(a) strike suits already filed (routine), and the **ARIKAYCE sNDA PDUFA of 28-Jan-2027 falling inside the deal window** — not deal-breaking under fixed cash, but the MAE carve-outs must be read. US pricing/tariff policy (Section 232, IRA) is now Sanofi's problem.
- **Value**: Probability-weighted IV **$95–105** (bear $36 / base $100 / bull $200) — the pre-deal price was 15–25% *above* intrinsic value; "excellent business, wrong price." Moat is real but a patent lease (Brinsupri NCE to 2030, LOE ~2037–38); 78% dilution in four years erodes per-share compounding.
- **Growth**: Best rare-disease launch of the decade — Brinsupri $0→$524M/qtr in 15 months (+268% YoY, 85.1% GM, four straight revenue beats, FCF burn narrowing −$294M→−$42M/qtr, near breakeven run-rate). Sanofi is buying at ~6.6x 2030E sales — **a bargain for the buyer, fully priced for the seller.** Verdict: hold existing, do not initiate.
- **Quantitative Signals**: Composite **NEUTRAL**. Value 2/100, Quality 8/100, Low-Vol 15/100; only momentum scores. R² vs SPY = 0.006 — the "+75% alpha" is statistically meaningless (t≈1.8); this was always a catalyst-driven binary stock, not a factor stock. Post-deal beta/vol figures are artefacts.
- **Financial Risk**: **MODERATE**, improving. Net cash ~$405M, current ratio 2.86x, **no debt maturity before Feb-2028**, first positive-EBIT quarter in Q2'26, breakeven revenue (~$2.16B) within ~3% of current run-rate. Altman Z −3.96 is a book-equity artefact, not a solvency signal. Still loss-making with −$658M TTM FCF — no cushion if the launch stalls on a break.
- **Non-Financial Risk**: **MODERATE, trending weak** — the memo's most important flags. (1) **Paul Hudson, former Sanofi CEO, was appointed an "independent" Insmed director on 20-Oct-2026, five weeks before signing** — recusal must be verified; (2) the Chief People Officer **sold $14.7M of stock on 19-Nov during live deal rumours** (10b5-1 plan adoption date is the key document); (3) shareholder approval requires **>2/3 of all outstanding shares with unvoted = NO** — the single largest completion risk; (4) $1.125B Insmed break fee disclosed but **Sanofi's reverse termination fee undisclosed** — antitrust break-risk allocation unknown.
- **ESG**: **AVERAGE / Neutral** — not a valuation input in a cash deal. Environmental profile genuinely low-risk (assured Scope 1+2). The standing social controversy is real: **ICER pegged Brinsupri's cost-effective price at $3.1–3.7k vs the $88k list (~25x gap)** — the key driver of break-scenario multiple compression, not the deal itself. Governance 6/10 (CEO/Chair duality, staggered board, 13% say-on-pay revolt).
- **Alternative Data**: Google Trends shows sustained Brinsupri interest with no post-launch decay (supports the floor valuation); tape is arb-dominated (79M shares, ~30x normal volume on announcement). Report was truncated — treated as low-weight corroboration only.
- **Short / Contrarian View**: **No edge — short thesis rejected.** Forensic work finds clean accounting (accruals −0.151, DSO flat at 45 days, no channel stuffing; Beneish flag is a mechanical hyper-growth artefact). The legitimate bear case (ICER pricing gap, two failed label expansions, 76% single-product concentration) is a *valuation* bear, not a *quality* bear — narrowing break downside to **$100–125**, not Value's $36 tail. Only actionable bear idea: vote-turnout failure, which would need DEFM14A evidence first.

---

**Bull Case**
- **Deal closes on terms (~90%+ probability)**: all-cash, committed financing, no financing condition, low antitrust overlap, strategic urgency on Sanofi's side (Dupixent succession). Holders collect $175 in ~6–7 months.
- **Topping-bid optionality (~5–8%)**: shareholder suits argue $175 undervalues the franchise; the board retains a fiduciary out; a $185–195 rival bid roughly doubles the return. Selling now forfeits this free option.
- **The floor is higher than the undisturbed price suggests**: clean accounting, 85% gross margins, near-breakeven run-rate, and the Sanofi bid itself re-rate standalone value toward $105–125 rather than the $93 June low.

**Bear Case**
- **Negative expected value versus cash**: at the market-implied ~92% completion rate, expected 7-month return ≈ 0% vs ~2.6% risk-free; the spread pays ~30–100bp to underwrite antitrust, turnout and litigation risk. Kelly criterion says size zero.
- **The vote is a real hurdle**: >2/3 of *outstanding* shares, unvoted = no, on a register with heavy passive/arb ownership — apathy can sink a deal the market assumes is done.
- **Process-integrity overhang**: ex-Sanofi CEO on the board during the sale, a $14.7M officer sale amid rumours, and an undisclosed reverse termination fee give plaintiffs a credible narrative and create small-but-real injunction/disclosure-delay risk to the H1-27 timeline (each quarter of slip costs ~1–1.5% of annualised return).

**Key Risks**
1. **Antitrust second request / EC Phase 2 referral** — collapses the timeline and the annualised spread (low probability, deal-defining).
2. **Shareholder vote failure** on the >2/3-of-outstanding, unvoted-equals-no threshold.
3. **Reverse termination fee proves nominal** — Sanofi walks cheaply on antitrust while INSM holders bear −30%.
4. **Sanofi credit/bridge stress** in a 5.13% 10Y, widening-spread tape — the load-bearing assumption of the cash consideration.
5. **Break scenario**: stock reverts to a long-duration launch story in a 3% real-rate world — $100–125, with PDUFA (28-Jan-27) and Brinsupri payer-access data as the swing factors.

**Portfolio Construction Note** (from the Portfolio Strategist)
- **New capital: 0% — PASS.** **Existing holders: reduce to a hard cap of 1.0%**; the position is dominated by T-bills at every completion probability below ~99%, and the all-cash structure makes it a taxable event regardless, so tax deferral is no reason to hold.
- **Reclassify the position out of biotech/growth into the event/cash sleeve** — INSM never provided biotech factor exposure (R² = 0.006) and now provides none at all; do not let the book think it owns biotech beta it has already sold.
- **Exit execution**: TWAP/VWAP over 3–5 sessions; liquidity is ample — capture the 2.85% spread to *exit*, not to hold. Do not scale into weakness: a dip toward $160 is the market raising break probability, not offering a discount.
- **Escalation triggers if any stub is retained**: $164 → re-underwrite; $158 → cut to 0.25%; $150 → exit in full. Immediate exit on: HSR second request, EC Phase 2, adverse DEFM14A disclosure on the 10b5-1 plan or Hudson recusal, Sanofi credit event, or a nominal reverse fee.
- **What would change the call**: a confirmed topping bid (hold to terms); a spread blow-out to 8–12% on *resolvable* litigation noise (genuine arb entry); disclosure of a large reciprocal Sanofi reverse fee (justifies up to 2%).

**Data gaps flagged**: merger agreement exhibits (reverse fee, outside date) not yet reviewed; CPO's 10b5-1 adoption date unknown; insider ownership unverified; Alt Data report truncated. These must be closed from the 8-K/DEFM14A before treating $175 as a floor.

*Bottom line: the business earned the bid, and shareholders have been paid. The verdict is HOLD only in the narrow sense of letting existing positions run to $175 — there is no return left to underwrite, and capital above a 1% stub belongs in T-bills.*

# INSM — Portfolio Construction Recommendation

**Verified market state (24-Nov-2026 close):** $170.15, volume 78.9M (≈30x normal), against Sanofi's **$175.00 all-cash** offer. Undisturbed price **$119.80** (18-Nov). Gross spread **$4.85 / 2.85%**. 60-day realised vol 70.8% and beta 0.108 (both now artefacts of the event). News sentiment 0.895 — but 2 of 20 stories are shareholder-lawyer investigations, and every sell-side target in the feed ($154–$213) is **stale pre-deal** and must be discarded.

> **The governing fact: this is no longer an equity position. It is a 7-month, fixed-payout, binary event claim on Sanofi's cash, and I am sizing it as such.**

---

## 1. Agent Conviction Summary Table

| Agent | View | Conviction | Key Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sector Researcher** | Attractive sector / **no view on stock** | High | Orphan respiratory is structurally attractive (86.7% peer GM, ~14% CAGR), but explicitly states sector call ≠ INSM recommendation; relevant only for break-scenario downside ($93–$120) |
| **Geo Legal** | Neutral / deal-dependent | High | Zero EM/hotspot exposure; risk now binary: HSR + EC/Japan/UK clearance, §14(a) strike suits, PDUFA 28-Jan-27 inside the window. Ratings: **MEDIUM** risk, ~85–90% close |

| **Value Researcher** | **Price 15–25% above IV** | High | Prob-weighted IV **$95–105** (bear $36 / base $100 / bull $200). "Good business, wrong price." Entry only ≤$85 |
| **Growth Researcher** | Hold existing / **do not initiate** | High | Best rare-disease launch of the decade (+268% YoY, 85% GM), but "Sanofi's $175 capitalises the whole ASPEN-to-2030 curve." 0.1:1 reward/risk |
| **Fin Risk Analyst** | Moderate | Medium | Net cash $405M, no maturity until Feb-2028, current ratio 2.86x; Altman −3.96 is a book-equity artefact. Breakeven revenue ~$2.16B vs ~$2.10B run-rate — **within 3%** |
| **Nonfin Risk Analyst** | **Moderate, trending weak** | High | **Paul Hudson (ex-Sanofi CEO) appointed "independent" director 20-Oct-26, ~5 weeks pre-signing**; CPO sold $14.7M on 19-Nov *during deal rumours*; **>2/3-of-outstanding vote, unvoted = NO**; $1.125B break fee, reverse fee undisclosed |
| **Quant Analyst** | Neutral | Medium | Value 2/100, Quality 8/100, Low-Vol 15/100; R² vs SPY = **0.006**, so the +75% "alpha" is statistically meaningless (t≈1.8). Catalyst stock, not a factor stock |
| **Short Analyst** | **No edge — reject short** | High | Accounting is **clean** (accruals −0.151, DSO flat at 45 days, no channel stuffing). Real bear case = ICER's $88k vs $3.1–3.7k cost-effective price. Standalone break value **$100–125** |
| **ESG** | Neutral / no action | Medium | E = LOW (assured Scope 1+2), S = **HIGH** (25x price-to-ICER-value gap), G = 6/10 (CEO/Chair duality, staggered board, 13% say-on-pay revolt). Not a valuation input now |
| **Alt Data** | Deal-framing (report truncated) | Low | Confirmed arb-dominated tape; alt data now informs only completion probability, bump plausibility, break downside |

**Weighting note:** I weight most heavily the four agents whose evidence bears directly on the *remaining* payoff — **Macro, Nonfin Risk, Short, and Value** — and discount Quant (invalid earnings-revision signal, n=4 peer set) and Alt Data (truncated). Sector, Growth and ESG are excluded from the sizing decision because their own authors explicitly disclaim relevance to the current instrument.

---

## 2. Consensus Assessment: **SPLIT (fundamentals) / HIGH (mechanics)**

The split is not a disagreement about facts — it is a disagreement about *which question is being asked*:

- **Unanimous (11/11):** the Sanofi deal dominates; the equity is now a merger-arb instrument; the fundamental business is excellent; **do not initiate a new position.**
- **Unanimous (6/6 who ran the math):** the spread is thin and the payoff is asymmetric — +2.85% vs −30% to −35%.
- **Genuine split — business quality:** Growth says A-grade execution and a bargain *for Sanofi*; Value says 15–25% above intrinsic value and no margin of safety. **Both are right**: Sanofi is buying at ~6.6x 2030 sales, which is cheap for the buyer and fully priced for the seller. That is what a 46% control premium looks like. It resolves to "no alpha left," not to a directional call.
- **Resolved conflict (per my hierarchy rule):** Value's $95–105 IV would normally argue *short*. Short Analyst's forensic work — clean accruals, flat DSO, conservative revenue recognition — **kills that thesis**. Fraud/accounting risk takes precedence over valuation opinion, so the standalone bear case is a *valuation* bear, not a *quality* bear. That materially narrows the break-scenario downside to **$105–125**, not $36.

---

## 3. Position Sizing Recommendation

### **New capital: 0.0% — Pass.**

### **Existing holders: reduce to a hard cap of 1.0% of portfolio.**

**The arithmetic that drives this.** Using the break value of ~$112 (midpoint of Short's $100–125 and Value's $95–105, marked up for the strategic-scarcity read-through from the Sanofi bid):

| Completion prob. | Expected gross return (7.2 months) | vs 26-wk T-bill (4.49% → 2.60%) |
|---|---|---|
| 92.3% (**market-implied**) | **+0.01%** | **−2.6%** |
| 95% | +1.01% | −1.6% |
| 97% | +1.74% | −0.9% |
| 99% | +2.32% | −0.3% |

**Holding INSM is dominated by T-bills at every plausible completion probability short of ~99%.** The market-implied 92.3% is itself roughly the *correct* base rate for a committed-financing, no-financing-condition, low-overlap strategic deal — so there is no mispricing to harvest, in either direction.

**Risk-budget check at a 3% weight** (the size a "high-conviction biotech" would normally carry):
- Spread capture: 2.85% × 3% = **+8.5bp** of portfolio
- Break hit: 7.7% × −34% × 3% = **−79bp** of portfolio
- Net expected: **≈ −0bp**, with a fat left tail and 7 months of illiquidity

You are running a 79bp downside risk to earn 8.5bp. That is a 1:9 risk/reward on a near-zero expected value — indefensible in a return-seeking sleeve.

**Kelly check:** f* = (p·b − q)/b where b = 2.85%, q = 7.7% → f* is **negative**. Kelly says size zero. The only legitimate positive size is a *topping-bid option* (see §6), which caps the position at 1.0%.

**Why 1.0% and not 0% for existing holders:** transaction costs, index-fund constraints where selling forces an off-benchmark rebalancing cost, and the ~5–8% probability of a $185–195 topping bid (the $1.125B break fee deters but does not eliminate it; the board retains a fiduciary out). Beyond 1.0%, the position is an unintended concentration with no compensating return.

**Critically: the tax-deferral argument for holding is weak.** The consideration is **all cash**, so the position is a taxable event in H1-2027 regardless. Selling now defers nothing but ~7 months of tax timing. That removes the single strongest conventional reason to sit in a thin arb.

---

## 4. Portfolio Fit Analysis

**Sector:** Healthcare/biotech line item becomes **misleading**. Post-deal, INSM is a short-duration USD cash claim with Sanofi counterparty risk. Risk reporting must **reclassify it out of biotech growth exposure into the event/cash sleeve**, or the fund will believe it holds biotech beta it has already sold.

**Factor exposure — the key insight:** INSM's pre-deal R² vs SPY was **0.006** and correlation to XBI was **0.386** (Quant). It never provided biotech factor exposure — it was pure idiosyncratic jump risk that *diversified nothing* and *hedged nothing*. Post-deal, that jumps to a binary completion risk **correlated with nothing in the book** — which looks diversifying on a correlation matrix but is a fat left tail. Do not let a low-correlation number justify the position.

**Concentration / look-through:** Owning INSM is economically **short Sanofi credit + long deal completion**. If the fund holds other large-cap pharma M&A paper, this stacks deal-break risk. If the fund holds SNY equity, the position is a partial offset (fine, but not a reason to own it).

**Rate / duration:** The claim's duration collapses from ~15 years (pre-deal biotech multiple) to **~0.6 years**, at a 5.13% 10Y / 4.37% front end. There is genuine opportunity cost: at a 10% equity hurdle, 7 months of capital at 4.7% annualised forgoes **~310bp** of return, ≈1.8% on the position's capital.

**Liquidity:** Not a constraint (2–3M shares/day normal; 79M on the event day), so exit is executable without market impact — which removes the usual "we're trapped" defence for holding.

---

## 5. Entry Strategy

**New money: no entry at any price above $168.** A new position is only justifiable at a spread wide enough to pay for the tail — i.e. **$160 or below** (implied p ≈ 76%, an 8.5%+ gross spread), which only occurs if the market starts pricing a genuine clearance problem. At that point it becomes a *deliberate* distressed-arb trade requiring a dedicated mandate, not a growth allocation.

**Existing holders exiting:** use a **TWAP/VWAP over 3–5 sessions**, not a single block and not a limit at $174.90 (which will not fill reliably and signals desperation to the arb community). Liquidity is ample; capture the 2.85% spread to *exit* rather than to hold.

**Do not scale in on weakness.** Any dip toward $160 is the market raising break probability, not a discount — you would be adding to a deteriorating event, not buying a cheaper business.

---

## 6. Risk Management Rules

**Price stop / escalation triggers (if any position is retained):**
- **$164** → spread >6.3%: re-underwrite. Verify no HSR second request, no EC Phase 2 referral.
- **$158** → implied p < 70%: **cut to 0.25%**. Something has broken in the process.
- **$150** → exit in full. At this level the market is pricing a coin-flip; do not "wait for the vote."

**Fundamental / event invalidation conditions (any one → exit immediately, ignore price):**
1. **HSR second request** or **EC referral to Phase 2** — the PTAB—sorry, the process timeline to H1-2027 becomes unachievable, and the annualised spread collapses to zero.
2. **DEFM14A reveals the CPO's (Schaeffer Orlov) 10b5-1 plan was adopted *after* 18-Nov** — this converts a routine strike suit into a credible insider-trading and process-integrity problem, with a real (if small) injunction risk to the vote.
3. **Board fails to confirm Paul Hudson's full recusal** from all deal deliberations, or his independence determination is qualified.
4. **Sanofi credit event:** downgrade, bridge take-out failure, or HY OAS gapping >500bp — the "secured committed financing" is the deal's load-bearing assumption.
5. **Reverse termination fee proves nominal (or absent)** — if Sanofi can walk on antitrust cheaply while INSM holders bear −34%, the risk is structurally mispriced and any position must go to zero.

**Trim / monetisation triggers (upside):**
- **$180+ (spread >2.8% *above* deal price):** a confirmed second bidder → hold to $185–190 only; an *unconfirmed* rumour → sell into it.
- **A rival offer or a raised Sanofi bid:** take the money. Do not hold for a bidding war in a stock with a $1.125B break fee and a >2/3 vote hurdle.

**Watch list (dated):** ARIKAYCE **PDUFA 28-Jan-2027** (inside the window — a CRL is not deal-breaking under fixed cash, but read the MAE carve-out); shareholder vote date; HSR early-termination notice.

---

## 7. Final Portfolio Action: **PASS (new capital) / REDUCE to ≤1.0% (existing)**

**Rationale in one line:** The Sanofi deal is more likely than not to close (~92%), but at $170.15 the residual 2.85% spread **does not pay for a −34% tail**, leaving an expected return of approximately zero over 7 months against 2.6% risk-free — a position that is Dominated by cash, misclassified as biotech exposure, and carries a documented process-integrity conflict (ex-Sanofi CEO on the board during the sale; an officer sale during live rumours).

**What would change my mind — and I want to be explicit, because the specialists are split:**
- A **topping bid** at $185+ transforms the payoff and justifies holding to terms.
- A spread blow-out to **8–12% ($155–162)** on a *resolvable* scare (litigation noise, not a second request) makes this a genuine, well-paid arb.
- Disclosure of a **large reciprocal Sanofi reverse termination fee** would meaningfully improve the risk allocation and would justify up to 2%.

Absent those, the honest answer to "should we own INSM?" is: **the business earned the bid; the shareholders have been paid; there is no return left to collect.**

**For the memo:** the standalone value of the franchise — $95–105 per the Value Researcher, $100–125 per the Short Analyst — is the number that matters if this deal breaks. That is the −35% anchor, and it should be written into the risk log next to the position, not the $175 headline.

---

## 1. Sector Overview

INSM competes in **commercial-stage orphan respiratory biotech**, a sub-sector defined by high-gross-margin, single-mechanism therapies sold into small, high-unmet-need patient populations through concentrated specialty distribution. The core addressable market — non-CF bronchiectasis — was only **~$1.6B across the 7 major markets in 2025** but is forecast to compound at **~13.7–15% through 2036** as the first approved mechanism (DPP-1 inhibition) creates a category from what was previously supportive care only; the US is the largest single market. The structural driver of the whole sub-sector right now is **big-pharma patent-cliff anxiety**: the 2026 US exclusivity wave has turned commercial-stage rare-disease assets with de-risked Phase 3 data into scarce strategic inventory, which is precisely the dynamic that produced the $41B Sanofi bid (Sanofi explicitly framing it as growth beyond Dupixent). Competitive intensity within the niche is **low today but rising** — first-to-market confers standard-of-care positioning, while class followers and neutrophil-pathway competitors are in mid/late-stage development.

*Data-integrity note: the sector-aggregate endpoint was unreliable (it returned 1-company periods for 2026). The one usable row — the 25 largest healthcare names, FY2025 — shows **$2.448T revenue, 61.1% gross margin, $275.2B net income (11.2% net margin)**. The `get_sector_peers` endpoint returned mega-cap diversified pharma (LLY, JNJ, ABBV, MRK) which is the wrong comp set for a $37B single-franchise orphan biotech; I substituted a hand-built rare-disease commercial biotech peer set.*

---

## 2. Key Tailwinds

- **Category creation with no incumbent.** Brinsupri (brensocatib) received FDA approval **12 Aug 2025** as the *first and only* approved therapy for non-CF bronchiectasis — a greenfield mechanism with no approved competitor to displace, and standard-of-care positioning already being described by analysts post-ATS 2026. The underlying 7MM market is small ($1.6B) but compounding ~14–15%, meaning share gains come from **treatment-naïve patients, not price wars**.
- **Violent operating leverage now visible in the P&L.** Revenue scaled **$107M (Q2'25) → $142M (Q3'25) → $264M (Q4'25) → $306M (Q1'26) → $425M (Q2'26) → $524M (Q3'26)**, i.e. +23% QoQ in the latest quarter. Quarterly operating loss collapsed from **−$366M (Q3'25)** to **−$1.5M (Q2'26)** and **−$89M (Q3'26)**. TTM gross margin is **84.3%** — essentially at rare-disease peer parity — so incremental revenue drops through at very high contribution.
- **A seller's market for de-risked orphan assets.** With Dupixent concentration risk and 2026-format patent cliffs, large-cap pharma is paying strategic premiums for approved, launch-phase respiratory franchises. INSM captured a **46% premium / ~27x TTM sales** — a valuation unavailable to a standalone mid-cap in a risk-off tape (the stock was **−57% from its Dec-2025 high** as recently as June 2026).

---

## 3. Key Headwinds

- **Payer power is the binding constraint, not clinical demand.** Specialty respiratory pricing faces IRA Medicare negotiation, PBM gross-to-net compression and step-edits/utilization management. With a **first-in-class premium price into a newly defined category**, realized net price (not volume) is the key swing variable — and it is set by buyers with far more leverage than a single-product seller.
- **Franchise concentration plus a 2030 exclusivity horizon.** Both commercial assets (ARIKAYCE, Brinsupri) are respiratory and both are Insmed-only. ARIKAYCE carries **17 US patents (14 active, 3 lapsed)** and has faced IP challenge; Brinsupri's NCE exclusivity runs only to **2030**, with DPP-1-class followers in development. There is no diversification cushion if either erodes.
- **Cost base is still launch-scale, and the market is diagnosis-limited.** SG&A plus R&D runs roughly **$450M/quarter** (SG&A $253M, R&D ~$193M in Q3'26), interest expense ~$20M/quarter, and TTM net loss is **−$606M**. Bronchiectasis is chronically under-diagnosed, so TAM realization depends on a slow, expensive physician-education/diagnostic-infrastructure build rather than simple penetration.
